offlineProtection.explainerLead: You must keep your dashboard or kitchen screen on and online during service.
offlineProtection.explainerBody: If the screen goes off, the device loses internet, or you switch to another website, offline protection takes over — either pausing ordering or turning auto-accept off, whichever you chose.
offlineProtection.reminder: ⚠️ Keep your dashboard or kitchen screen on and online during service, or offline protection may take over.
offlineProtection.enableConfirm:
Offline protection enabled.

To keep orders flowing, your screen must stay on. If this device loses connection, offline protection takes over in the mode you chose.

Make sure Screen On is enabled on this device.
offlineProtection.disableConfirm:
Disable offline protection for this event?

If this device loses connection, online orders will continue — customers may place orders you cannot see. Only disable if you have a reliable connection.
offlineProtection.cardDescription: Decides what happens to incoming orders when your device drops offline.
offlineProtection.purpose: If your device loses its connection, this stops orders arriving while you can’t see them.
offlineProtection.switchHelp: What happens when this van loses its connection.

pause.label: Pause online ordering
pause.help: Customers can’t order until you’re back online.

no_auto_accept.label: Keep taking orders, confirm them yourself
no_auto_accept.help: Auto-accept is turned off, so customers can still order but nothing is confirmed automatically. You’ll confirm each one when you’re back online — and anything still waiting is rejected automatically after your selected time, with the customer emailed to let them know.

kitchenCapacity.desc: The most items your kitchen can turn out at once, across all the categories you’ve ticked. Each category’s own batch size still applies on top.
kitchenCapacity.example: Example: if you can cook 4 mains in 5 minutes, then set it to 4 items every 5 minutes. The total capacity limits orders across all selected categories so if you want to only sell a maximum of 10 starters and mains every 5 minutes, then set Total capacity to 10 items every 5 minutes and tick the Starters and Mains boxes. This will still keep your mains restricted to 4 items every 5 minutes.
kitchenCapacity.noLimit: Leave at the infinity symbol for no limit.
kitchenCapacity.warning: ⚠️ For kitchen capacity to work properly, set a prep time and batch size on your menu categories (Menu & Stock). Without them, capacity can’t tell how long items take to cook.
kitchenCapacity.noVan: Add a van in Settings › Truck settings to set your kitchen capacity.
kitchenCapacity.lead: How many items your kitchen can make, so customers can only pick collection times you can meet.
kitchenCapacity.sameForAll: Same kitchen capacity for all vans?
kitchenCapacity.confirmBody: All vans will use {van}’s kitchen capacity. Each van’s own numbers will be replaced.
kitchenCapacity.colCountsTitle: Which categories count toward the total capacity. Cooked categories always count; tick instant ones (sides, dips, drinks) to include them.
kitchenCapacity.countsLocked: Cooked — always counts (its prep & batch set the pace)
kitchenCapacity.countsNoCap: Set a capacity to choose which categories count
kitchenCapacity.countsUnavailable: Unavailable until the database is updated
kitchenCapacity.countsTick: Tick to include this instant category (sides, dips, drinks) in the shared per-window limit
kitchenCapacity.setCapacityFirst: Set a capacity to choose which categories count.
kitchenCapacity.categoryBatchAria: {hasCategory, select, yes {{category} items per batch} other {items per batch}}
kitchenCapacity.categoryPrepAria: {hasCategory, select, yes {{category} prep time} other {prep time}}
kitchenCapacity.prepPerOrderHelp: How long one order takes to prepare
kitchenCapacity.itemsAtATimeHelp: How many items your kitchen can cook simultaneously
kitchenCapacity.instantNote: Instant items don’t count towards kitchen capacity — customers receive them immediately.

allowCancellation.label: Allow customers to cancel orders
allowCancellation.sentence: Customers can cancel up to <select></select> before their pickup time

autoAccept.label: Auto-accept orders
autoAccept.help: Orders confirm automatically. If the requested slot is full, the order bumps to the next available slot. Only confirms when there is capacity. Orders with customer notes (e.g. an allergy) will still need to be confirmed.

orderReady.label: Order-ready step
orderReady.help: Show a “Mark ready” button on the orders screen. Kitchen screens are set separately, on each device. Customers are emailed whenever an order is marked ready. Applies to all events — you can still turn it on or off for a single event on its dashboard.

buzzers.label: Do you hand out buzzers for collection?
buzzers.help: Record which buzzer you gave each customer, so you know who to look for when their food is ready.
buzzers.countLabel: How many buzzers do you have?

whereYouTrade.stepIntro: This sets your currency, prices, time zone and phone format. The country can’t be changed later, because it’s tied to your card payments.
whereYouTrade.countryGuessed: We guessed this from where you are. Change it if it’s wrong.
whereYouTrade.townQuestion: Town or city you’re based in
whereYouTrade.saveFailed: Couldn’t save settings — please try again.

stockCopy.defaultScopeNote: Default for every event. To set a different amount for one event, change it on that event’s dashboard — events you’ve already set there keep their own amount.

allergenMode.perDishBody: Review every dish and confirm its allergens. Customers see per-dish tags plus an allergen summary card derived from them.
allergenMode.cardBody: Upload or paste a single allergen card (PDF, image, or text), shown as-is. Per-dish tags stay hidden.

walkthrough.title: New to HatchGrab?
walkthrough.body: A quick tour of what lives on each tab. Takes about a minute.

getApp.title: Get the app
getApp.body: The kitchen app runs your service on a phone or tablet — and it is the only way to keep taking orders when you lose signal. Free with your account, on iPhone, iPad and Android.

logo.label: Logo
logo.removeConfirm: Remove your logo? Customers will see your truck name without it. You can upload a new one at any time.
logo.removeFailed: Couldn’t remove the logo — please try again.

contact.addEmailOrPhone: Add an email or phone above to offer a contact method.
contact.tickWhatsApp: ⚠️ Tick “This number is on WhatsApp” on the Phone field to use WhatsApp.

schedule.title: Your schedule
schedule.autoDesc: Tell us where you post your schedule and we’ll check it for you, sending any events we find for your approval. This needs to be your own website — not a Facebook or Instagram page.
schedule.eitherWay: Either way, if we find your events listed elsewhere, we’ll still send these to you for approval. Nothing goes live until you confirm it.
schedule.wherePost: Where do you post your schedule?
schedule.checkingHelp: This can take up to 2 minutes — please keep this page open and don’t close the tab.
schedule.urlHelp: Your website where customers can see your upcoming events — not a Facebook or Instagram page
schedule.exclusionsHelp: These terms are automatically filtered out when importing your schedule. Remove any that were added by mistake.

qr.title: Order QR code
qr.domainLive: This QR code now sends customers to <mono>{domain}</mono>. You never need to print a new one.
qr.domainNotLive: This QR code sends customers to your HatchGrab ordering page. If you set up your own web address later, the same QR code will send them there instead — you will not need to print a new one.
qr.printHelp: Print or display this code so customers can scan and pre-order. Place it at your hatch, on your van, or share it online.
qr.noUrl: No order link yet — your truck’s page address isn’t set.
qr.brandedHelp: Your logo shown in the middle of the QR code
qr.addLogo: Add your logo to your profile and it will show here.
qr.lockedTitle: Branded codes are switched off for your truck
qr.lockedBody: Branded codes are switched off for your truck. Your standard QR code works exactly the same for customers — the difference is your logo in the middle.

accounts.title: For your accountant
accounts.help: Sales count on the day of the event. Gross is what customers paid. Net is what is left after refunds and tax.
accounts.taxNone: No tax rate is set for your truck, so no tax is worked out here.
accounts.coverage: {total, plural, one {Cost set for {withCost} of # dish sold} other {Cost set for {withCost} of # dishes sold}}
accounts.partial: Dishes without a cost are left out of the cost, so this profit is higher than it really is. Add a cost to each dish in Menu.
accounts.noCosts: No dish has a cost yet. Add a cost to your dishes in Menu to see your profit.
accounts.eventNoProfit: A dash means not every dish sold there has a cost.
accounts.downloadHelp: Two spreadsheet files: one row for each order, and one row for each event. They open in Excel, Numbers, Xero and QuickBooks.
